Hi Liam — thanks for flagging this.

Quick checks: could you try the link in an incognito/private window and confirm the browser + version? If your org's email is behind an email proxy that rewrites links, that can sometimes strip relaystate on the SSO handoff and result in a blank page.

I’ve looped in Rachel from our onboarding ops so we can look at the invite record and reissue a temporary accept link if needed.

Next steps from our side:
- Rachel will check the invite delivery headers and whether the relaystate/token was intact.
- If the invite expired or got mangled we’ll send a one-time temporary activation link that bypasses the usual redirect for troubleshooting.

Can you share the browser + OS? If you can forward the original email (if it exists) that would help us confirm whether links were rewritten in transit.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Forwarding invite record details and headers I pulled from the system:
- Invite sent: 2027-04-04T18:07:13Z
- Invite token ID: tok_7f9c2b_relay_33
- Destination: https://coupa.redwood-inference.com/accept?token=tok_7f9c2b_relay_33
- Delivery path: SES -> customer mail gateway -> delivered

I checked the MIME and it looks like the link arrived intact to GreenArk's MX; however the click tracking redirect step shows an HTTP 302 to our SSO endpoint and then a 200 with empty HTML body (reported by our CDN logs). That pattern aligns with a relaystate drop on the Okta assertion.

Attaching the delivery headers and the screenshot Ben mentioned.
Attachment: invite-delivery-headers.txt (text, 6 KB)

Marissa — can you advise whether we should temporarily reissue an activation link that uses a one-time token and skips the click-tracking redirect? We did that once for a customer with a proxy that strips querystrings.

Rachel
